RagShortTexts: Javelin fighters choose engagement by distance and terrain.
Equipment and mobilization depend on households and leaders.

Variants.Content: Light Lithuanian javelin fighters throw at suitable distance, then regroup or withdraw with companions and terrain. Weapons may not be recovered; shields and provisions limit carrying. Local familiarity works through watches and coordinated movement.
After throwing, a fighter watches companions and exits rather than the landing alone. Unfamiliar pursuit scatters formation, especially after spare missiles are spent.
Light troops still cost food, shields and shafts. Repeated farm absences weaken replenishment, while repair and practice consume time.
A household loses a worker and funds repairs. If returns favor only leaders, suppliers and relatives guarding home have little reason to support another levy.
